name: Christiane Amanpour
bio: Christiane Amanpour CBE is a British-Iranian journalist and television host who serves as CNN's Chief International Anchor and host of PBS's Amanpour & Company. With fearless reporting from conflict zones including the Gulf War, the Bosnian War, and the Rwandan genocide, she earned international acclaim for holding global warlords and politicians accountable. Her unflinching dedication to factual journalism has garnered virtually every major broadcast journalism honor.

faq.q: What war made Christiane Amanpour internationally recognized?
faq.a: Her fearless, truthful frontline reporting during the Bosnian War and the Siege of Sarajevo in the early 1990s cemented her global reputation.
She famously insists: 'We must be truthful, not neutral. Being neutral between the victim and the aggressor is not being objective; it's complicity.'

name: Walter Cronkite
nickname: Uncle Walter / The Most Trusted Man in America
bio: Walter Leland Cronkite Jr. was an American broadcast journalist who served as anchorman for the CBS Evening News for 19 years from 1962 to 1981. In an opinion poll during his heyday, he was cited as 'the most trusted man in America' for his steady, authoritative, and impartial delivery. Cronkite anchored historic moments in human history including the assassination of John F. Kennedy, the Apollo 11 Moon landing, and the Vietnam War.

famousWorks.title: Battle of the Bulge reporting as WWII combat correspondent
Live television broadcast announcing the assassination of President JFK
Editorial broadcast questioning the Vietnam War following the Tet Offensive
CBS live broadcast coverage of Apollo 11's Moon landing

faq.q: What was Walter Cronkite's famous sign-off catchphrase?
faq.a: He concluded his CBS Evening News broadcasts with: 'And that's the way it is...'

faq.q: How did Cronkite's 1968 Vietnam commentary affect President Lyndon B. Johnson?
faq.a: President Johnson famously remarked: 'If I've lost Cronkite, I've lost Middle America.'
